category_title: Verbal student with ASD and hyperactivity with high musical engagement and sensitivity to stimuli
minimal_context: The student is preparing to have his daily food and drinks in the classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for your snack. We do not have your regular juice today, so please drink this different juice instead.

STUDENT: (Spins a straw in one hand while holding a toy in the other hand) No, I drink the same juice every day.

TUTOR: You need to drink this one today. Go ahead and try it.

STUDENT: (Starts to cry) No! I eat the same food and drink the same juice every day at school!

TUTOR: We don't have it right now. Please stop crying and sit at your desk.

STUDENT: (Cries uncontrollably and starts screaming. He throws himself on the floor and begins punching his head.)

options.A: Create social story lyrics following current guidelines and set them to the melody of the student's favorite song.
options.B: Vary classroom activities by including more active learning strategies, including cooperative learning groups during snack time.
options.C: Provide a clear beginning and end for each classroom activity, such as taking food and drinks.
options.D: Provide support during snack time in small groups of three to five students or individually outside the classroom.
